t: The Rashidun Caliphate was the rule of the first four caliphs after the Prophet Muhammad, from Medina, in 632–661.
In about 25 years it destroyed the Sasanian Empire and took Syria and Egypt from Byzantium, setting Arabic on its path to dominance.
Disputes over succession led to the murders of three caliphs and civil war, ending in the hereditary Umayyad Caliphate.
dyk: Umar adopted the Islamic lunar calendar for official dating, anchoring it to the hijra of 622, the system still used in the Muslim world today.
ev: Abu Bakr is acclaimed first caliph after Muhammad's death and launches the Ridda Wars
Umar ibn al-Khattab succeeds Abu Bakr and accelerates the conquests
Khalid ibn al-Walid and Abu Ubayda defeat the Byzantines at the Yarmuk
Victory at Nihawand breaks the last organised Sasanian field army
Rebels assassinate Uthman, triggering the First Fitna
Ali and Muawiya fight the inconclusive Battle of Siffin
Ibn Muljam assassinates Ali at Kufa; the Umayyad Caliphate follows
